interface.evidence: Original problem lists only input in (8 bits) and output pos (3 bits).

semantics.function: For nonzero in, pos is the smallest bit index i with in[i] equal to 1; for zero in, pos is zero.
semantics.timing: Combinational, with no added clock, reset, state, or cycle latency: original problem describes an input-vector priority encoder and supplies no clock/reset ports.
semantics.initialization: No initial output value is specified; verify after driving a defined input and allowing combinational settling.
semantics.example: 8'b10010000 maps to 3'd4 per the original problem.

numeric.output_range: Unsigned bit index 0 through 7, represented in 3 bits
numeric.priority: Bit 0 has highest priority; bit 7 has lowest priority.
numeric.zero: Zero input and any input with bit 0 set both report 0.

verification.oracle: Independently scan original-spec input indices from 7 down to 0, overwriting expected index on each set bit, leaving the least significant set index; default expected zero.
verification.coverage: Exhaust all 256 binary inputs in ascending and descending order, including zero, each one-hot input, all ones, and original example.
verification.sampling: Drive input then wait 1 ns before checking output with case inequality.
verification.completion: Fatal on mismatches, bounded timeout, PASS line only after all checks; run fixed dev_check.py initial.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: Original specification defines high bits and binary example but no X/Z behavior.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Do not impose an X/Z oracle; verify the full binary domain.
